### 8.2 Classification discipline

`PROVEN` means direct evidence at the cited ref; `DECIDED` means an effective governing record; `INFERRED` is not used to create any identity or authority; `UNPROVEN` means evidence is absent or insufficient; `CONFLICTING` records incompatible source/status claims without resolving them by assumption; `DEFERRED` means the governing F-3 scope excludes the capability for now. Persistence fit, identity binding, qualification, implementation authority, acceptance, product admission, route/UI enablement, publication, and remote verification remain distinct layers.

The commit/merge ancestry, manifest contract, destination path and actual bounded coverage are consistent.

**PR disposition.** PR [#96](https://github.com/ramkivs/iips-review-recovered/pull/96), base `main`, head `arena/63a310bc-iips-review-recovered` at the exact transfer commit, was **MERGED** at `2026-10-14T09:20:37Z` as merge commit `f813354092b9e926ad93fb06080a7d64465aa4ae`. # PART II — CONSOLIDATED CONVERGENCE REGISTER AND FORWARD PLAN (`2026-10-14`, independent re-establishment)

*Prepared in a fresh Arena session on branch `arena/ee3fd321-iips-review-recovered`. Additive consolidation: this section creates **no** new decision, lifts **no** fence, authorizes **no** implementation, and does **not** replace §§1–15 or any governed record. Where this section and §§1–15 disagree on a *decision*, §§1–15 govern; where they disagree on an *observable repository fact*, the live re-verification recorded at §16.3 governs and the earlier text is corrected additively.*

## 16.1 Purpose, method and reading order

**Purpose.** Establish, from the repositories themselves, what the IIPS application is, what is actually complete and verified across IRR and IPD, what is genuinely unfinished, which items actually prevent convergence, what can proceed in parallel, and the shortest safe route to a coherent, usable single-user application.

**Method used in this session.** Read the authoritative records (§§1–15, the `docs/integration` decision corpus, `program-v1.1-certification/`, IPD `docs/`+`evidence/`+ the IPD XLSX program tracker), then independently re-verify the consequential facts against the live repositories and by **executing the application** in this sandbox (fresh `npm ci`, typecheck, full test suite, production build, live HTTP probe of every served route, journal write, and branch-reachability analysis). No prior session's reported state was accepted as proof of current state where the repository could be checked directly.

**Reading order for a newcomer:** §17 (executive view) → §18 (capability matrix) → §19 (pending work) → §20 (ordered progression) for the structured view; and for the underlying record trail §16.2 → §16.3 → §16.4 → §16.5 → §16.6 → §16.7 (§16.7.1 decisions, §16.7.2 per-capability paths) → §16.8 → §16.9–§16.10 (boundaries and limits) → §16.11 → §16.12 → §16.13/§16.14 (corrections applied to this section).

## 16.2 What the application is (plain English)

IIPS is a **personal investment-research and portfolio-intelligence workbench** for a single owner-operator, running **non-production** on that person's own machine. Two repositories, one product:

| Layer | Repository | What it contributes |
|---|---|---|
| Application + certified analytics | `ramkivs/iips-review-recovered` (IRR) | React/Vite UI shell (24 leaf routes; 5 named surfaces plus the wildcard honestly render a "not yet built" placeholder); a first-party HTTP transport (`frontend/server/executive-transport.ts`, default `:8787`) that runs the certified 13-sector engine platform **in-process**; durable owner-scoped surfaces (watchlists, collaboration, settings) on an append-only NDJSON journal; governed screener; evidence/snapshot/replay browsing; AI explanation over certified results |
| Data-plane library + operator console | `ramkivs/iips-production-market-data` (IPD) | Canonical contracts, security master / identity resolution, normalization, quality, point-in-time (PIT) store and read service, fundamentals, intelligence data, broker-CSV import, plus an offline operator UI shell whose server-coupled surfaces are honestly fail-closed |

**Compute model.** Sector engines (IES-006…015, 016, 017, 020 — 13 certified) produce deterministic `EngineOutput`s over a **frozen replay baseline**; the Cross-Sector Intelligence Pipeline composes them; the transport serves 1:1 DTOs. The UI is presentation-only and never recomputes a decision. Reference analytics are labelled `freshness: SNAPSHOT` (`calibratedAt 2026-08-09`).

**Ownership model.** No authentication, no login, no roles, no tenants as a product concept. Durability is partitioned by a **server-owned owner-context carrier** (`IIPS_OWNER_CONTEXT_PATH` → a 363-byte JSON file that must match a pinned SHA-256 and the approved `(owner-7f3a91c2, irr-domain-4b82d6e1)` pair) resolved per request, uncached. If the carrier is absent or invalid, every owner-scoped operation answers HTTP `503 owner-context-unavailable`; nothing is inferred and no fallback owner exists.

| 2 | **User Portfolio admission** (the capability, per `G-2`) | first a PA act authorizing **re-qualification** (and, if chosen, a bounded residual implementation act) plus the **non-authentication ownership source** designation; **admission is a further separate act** that alone lifts `D-1`/record §8.5 — CV-20 → CV-52 (readiness/implementation records already exist: V16) | CV-50 (a closed path is not a prerequisite); the runbook, pins, IPD test runner |

| 4 | **Real-security coverage on durable surfaces** | the governed-universe scope question — CV-22 (identity/security-master domain, resolvable on IPD `main`'s existing `SecurityMaster`/D05 per `G-2` §2) | CV-20, CV-21, CV-50 (store choice cannot widen the universe) |

## 16.7 Forward plan (dependency-linked work packages)

No predetermined phases, and no single gating decision: WP-1, WP-2 and WP-3 are mutually independent and independent of every decision; **WP-4** holds three *separate* questions (portfolios / Reports / universe); **WP-4b** is the portfolio chain’s entry act — narrowed, on V16 evidence, to the **admission + ownership-source decision** rather than a fresh readiness study; **WP-5** executes only what its own authority acts grant; **WP-6** closes named leftovers. ### 16.7.1 The precise outstanding questions (no manufactured dependencies; nothing here re-opens `G-2`)

**Q1 (CV-20) — what does the PA authorize for the already-implemented, unadmitted durable portfolio line?**
The three acts in this chain are **separate and ordered**: (i) authorization to work the evidence — qualification (re-verification) and, if wanted, a bounded residual implementation act; (ii) the recorded **qualification** result; (iii) a later, distinct **admission** act naming commits and boundaries. Q1 is only (i) plus the ownership-source designation — it cannot grant (iii) by implication, and no option below does.
- **A. Authorize the qualification sequence only (the recommended default).** *Content:* re-qualify the durable line (`470cc698…`) at the rebased tree — its recorded evidence is targeted `59/59` and a full-suite "+59 with zero new failures" measured against the 2026-10-07 baseline, and the branch is **`149` commits behind** `main` (V17) — plus the executed restart-durability and idempotence proofs `G-2` §3 demands. *Consequence:* the admission decision then rests on current evidence; nothing is admitted, pinned, promoted or un-fenced by this act, and it authorizes no product-code change of any kind — implementation would require option B.²
- **B. Authorize A *and* a bounded residual implementation act.** *Content:* the same qualification mandate plus authority to implement only what the records leave unbuilt — durability behind IPD `main`’s in-memory `PortfolioStore` (CV-39) and the wiring of an admitted store, each inside the `G-2` §5 additive boundary. *Consequence:* closes the gap in one planning pass, but implementation authority stays narrower than admission: qualification (ii) must still be recorded, and **admission (iii) remains a separate later act**.²
- **C. Expressly defer, with a dated reason.** *Consequence:* the read surfaces stay fail-closed and are described as **implemented-but-unadmitted** (not "unbuilt"); WP-5 stays closed; nothing else in the plan is affected. Honest and complete on its own; the only cost is that owner-owned holdings stay fenced this cycle.
- **Deliberately not offered: "admit as-is" with a dated acceptance note.** The records leave no such shortcut. `D-1` keeps G24 main admission **prohibited**, the implementation record §8.5 withholds admission of its own act, and `AD-20`/Gate A with `P2`/`P3` hold a qualification bar that an admission act is required to rest on — so admitting `470cc698…` today would either bypass qualification or silently grant authority the records reserve separately, on a stale tree inheriting two failures `main` has since moved past. If the PA ever chooses admission, it is issued **after** (ii) as its own act naming the commits, the boundaries, the fence state and the qualification evidence it relies on.
- **Separable second act (accompanies A, B or C):** designate the **non-authentication ownership source** the `503` seam waits on — `frontend/server/user-portfolio-transport.ts` states it does not authenticate, synthesize a principal, pass credentials upstream or infer a tenant, and the implementation record §8.1–§8.2 deferrals are what keep the seam closed. Naming that source is a small, in-scope act and does **not** admit any lineage; **re-adding OIDC/Keycloak machinery to make the branch store admissible is not an option** (CV-50, terminal).
- **Not options at all:** selecting an IRR-owned portfolio store, reading `G-2` acceptance as implementation or admission authority (`G-2` §1/§5/§8/§9), or reviving the retired trust-anchor chain. Any change of *ownership* would require a subsequent, equally explicit PA architectural act, which this plan neither proposes nor assumes.

² A or B authorizes **evidence-gathering and, under B, narrower implementation**; neither is an admission act. Stage 5 in §20 states the exit criteria for each step separately.

**Q1a (CV-20) — within IPD ownership, which durable storage technology satisfies `G-2` §3?** Reserved to the PA, and properly **answered by the Stage 5 qualification evidence** (not by a guess now, and not by `WP-4b` — whose readiness output already exists on `main`, V16). `G-2` deliberately leaves storage technology unchosen; `6828155e` remains an `AD-03` reference designation, not an adopted store, and its OIDC-shaped trust model is out of scope (CV-50).

**Q1b (CV-20, XV-13) — how are the `G-2` §3 requirements read for a single-owner, non-production application?** Specifically "explicit owner/principal identity", "explicit tenant/company context", "server-side authorization" and "tenant and owner isolation": whether the already-governed F-3 partition semantics satisfy them (as they do for `NP-09/10/11`) or whether a differently stated in-scope mechanism is required. The **requirements themselves stay**; only their in-scope realization is open.

**Q2 (CV-21) — Reports:** retire from the v1 surface set / commission a bounded first-party design / retain deferral. Independent of Q1 by `G-2` §8; answering Q1 answers nothing here.

**Q3 (CV-22) — Governed universe (historical alternatives; answered 2026-10-19):** the PA selected **OPTION C — DEFER EXPANSION PENDING DEFINED PREREQUISITES** in the governing decision artifact. Preserve the 13-row IRR universe; do not expand to full D05 or infer a real-only subset. This current Option C is not the earlier PKG-04 Option C (“commission real-market coverage”), which remains unselected. The disposition does not permanently reject future D05 consumption.

**Q4 (CV-23) — Gate A necessity**; **Q5 (CV-25) — pin tagging (reproducibility, independent)**; **Q6 (CV-24) — `F6` inventory and `TD-7b`**.

**Work that may proceed now, regardless of Q1–Q6:** WP-1, WP-2 (tag approval only), WP-3, and CV-21/CV-22 documentation of their own status. **Work that must not:** any `P-4`/`P-6`/`P-8` step (CV-50 — closed path, not a to-do); implementation on the `G-2` path before its §9 readiness act and its own authority; IPD `main` promotion, re-pin or lineage merge; activation of `/api/user-portfolios*` or `/api/reports*`; any merge of the stale auth-era branches (XV-10).

### 16.7.2 Critical path and the smallest materially-advancing set

**Per-capability critical paths (there is no single one for "the application"):**
- *Coherent, usable today:* **WP-1 → WP-3 → WP-2** (runbook + start command + integrity + pin protection). No decision required; this is the whole distance between "verified repository" and "usable application" for everything that already works.
- *User Portfolios:* **Q1 (authorize the qualification act; a bounded residual implementation act only if chosen) → recorded qualification result → admission as its own later act** (`P2`/`P3`-equivalent, CV-52) → ownership-source designation and read-surface enablement, in that order (CV-20 → CV-39 → CV-52; V16/V17). Design and the non-production implementation are **not** outstanding — what is outstanding is qualification **at the current tree** and then admission, which no act in this register grants and no earlier option in this plan substitutes.
- *Reports:* **Q2 → R1/R2 → R3 → F-7 → UI port** (CV-21 → CV-51) — parallel to, never downstream of, the portfolio chain.
- *Real-security coverage:* **Q3** alone (CV-22) — independent of both, and the cheapest large usability gain.

**Smallest set that materially advances convergence:** the **WP-1 + WP-3 + WP-2 bundle** plus **one dated line per question Q1/Q2/Q3/Q5**. That bundle makes the existing verified product operable and trustworthy by a newcomer, and Q1–Q3 either close three capability questions or record them as deliberate boundaries. It is intentionally not "finish the portfolio chain": `G-2` §9 makes that a multi-act sequence, and no part of it may be compressed by an implementer.

## 16.8 Concrete acceptance criteria for "converged and usable" (product level)

1. Fresh clone → `npm ci` → `npm run build` → `tsc --noEmit` 0 → `vitest run` **703/703** (or the then-current count) with no manual source edits. *(Already met: V1–V4.)*
2. A newcomer following only the runbook starts the transport and UI and sees the 13-engine reference analytics, screener execution, evidence/replay, and can create + read a durable watchlist. *(Met once the runbook exists: V5, V6, V8 + CV-30.)*
3. Owner-scoped failure semantics remain honest and are *shown* as such: absent/invalid carrier → `503`, never a fabricated owner. *(Met: V7.)*
4. The consumed pin and the `AD-03` reference resolve to **tagged** commits; install reproducibility documented. *(CV-25 — protects every path above; it is not a prerequisite of any of them.)*
5. IPD `npm test` on a clean tree yields a real run or a non-zero exit. *(CV-35.)*
6. **User-portfolio coherence, expressed as `G-2` compliance rather than as a store choice:** either the fenced state is *stated in the UI and in this register* as a deliberate product boundary, or the `G-2` path is completed through its own acts **in order** — qualification recorded at the current tree, then admission by a separate act — and demonstrates every §3 element it claims — explicit owner scoping, stable portfolio identity, restart-durable persistence, versioned serialization, migration path, lifecycle/retention, reset/deletion, concurrency, isolation, auditability, contribution/lineage/idempotency preservation — with unresolved securities kept `UNRESOLVED` and the certified reference portfolio provably untouched (`G-2` §6/§7). *(CV-20 → Q1 → WP-4b → WP-5.)*
6a. **Reports coherence is judged separately** (CV-21): a stated boundary, or its own `R1`/`R2`/`R3`/`F-7` evidence. Portfolio admission never satisfies it.
6b. **Coverage:** for whatever Q3 selects, the accepted universe is stated and enforced identically across surfaces, with the real-name ceiling (52 of 2,250 under option B) disclosed rather than discovered by the user. *(CV-22.)*
7. No repository front-matter contradicts verified state (XV-1), and no gate record leaves an orphan "pending" where a disposition exists (§16.4.3 rows).
8. Cross-repo posture unchanged where protected: IRR fences byte-identical — `git hash-object` on `frontend/server/reports-transport.ts` = `981470541812a64c733309f1debec75455d85bee`, `frontend/server/user-portfolio-transport.ts` = `51704c12a467cd2f718a030b5036bc55c9afa73f`, `frontend/server/owner-context-unavailable.ts` = `cb8db45d668d28cee7e0a52721001d579a872733` (all three re-verified at `CV-CORR-01` on `2026-10-14`), tested 2F blobs unchanged, IPD refs unmoved unless an act says otherwise.

## 16.9 Scope exclusions and boundaries that must stay protected

Out of scope and **not** a prerequisite for anything above (per `H-18` and `GC-P2-SCOPE-CORR-01`): global authentication, OIDC/Keycloak, RBAC, multi-user and tenant infrastructure, enterprise authentication architecture, production activation, provider entitlements/live feeds.

Protected by existing authority, unchanged by this section: no re-opening of `REG-01…REG-13` dispositions; `GC-D1` operational prohibitions, `GC-D2` (2F) and `GC-D3…GC-D6` records stand as written; `P2`/`P3` admission, `AD-20` residual items, `D115-A` ineffectiveness, "no Company Identity Authority"; `/api/user-portfolios*` and `/api/reports*` stay `503`; `/api/pit/company/:companyId` stays unadmitted (`P4`); `phase14.1-recovery-deposit@c115d1f4` and the historical `program-v1.1.0` LTS stay preserved; frozen engine/calibration/certification artifacts are untouched; the retired auth/admin stack on stale branches must not re-enter `main` (XV-10); IPD `main` receives no promotion, re-pin or lineage merge without its own act.

No Windows claim is made here.

## 16.11 Original convergence assessment (current status superseded by §16.49)

**Current-status notice (`2026-10-18`).** This section preserves the earlier convergence framing; do not use its former pending-work list as current. CV-25, CV-35, and CV-42 are now complete for their recorded evidence scopes, as are CV-30/CV-31 and CV-41. Current item statuses and the outstanding-work count are in §§16.12, 16.49, and §19. The remaining qualification/admission, product-disposition, and human-reader/Windows/browser criteria are not inferred from those closures.

Short answer: **three small independent fixes make the verified product operable and honest; two capability questions and one authority act decide what the product may become.** No single item blocks the application.

1. Anyone can install and run the *research* product today, via a written path, and the two sidebar headings no longer dead-end (CV-30/CV-31/CV-41 — **closed by `CV-CORR-04`**, effective on publication to `main`). **Macro** is the parallel case: its read path runs but has no surface and cannot acquire one without the D89 gate (`CV-53`, §16.17).
2. **User Portfolios** are governed by an accepted `G-2` architecture whose non-production implementation **was authorized and completed** on 2026-10-07 but is **unadmitted and un-wired**: `G-2` §9’s withhold gave way only to that act (V16), IPD `main`’s store is in-memory (V15), and the only durable candidate sits on a branch `149` commits behind `main` (V17) whose one binding path is closed by scope (CV-50 — terminal record, not a prerequisite and not a gate). What is missing is the **next act in order** — authorize qualification, record its result, and only then decide admission as its own act — not a debate about ownership and not an admission shortcut.
3. **Reports** has a fence but no capability, and its deferral is its own (`REG-11` Option C, `G-2` §8 excludes it from the portfolio decision) — it should become a stated product boundary or its own scoped item (CV-21).
4. **Coverage** is the quietest and most user-visible gap: durable surfaces can only name 13 governed rows, so "add RELIANCE" fails (CV-22), and analytics are a frozen `SNAPSHOT` by certified design.
5. Two integrity traps and a stale-paper trail: an install that breaks if a branch moves (CV-25), a test command that can pass with zero tests (CV-35), a stale IPD program tracker (CV-36). The stale front-matter (CV-33/XV-1) is corrected by `CV-CORR-04`, pending publication; §16.17 adds a second cross-repo integrity note (XV-15: an unmounted IPD Macro builder that stamps `REAL` provenance with a placeholder lineage digest).

After 1 and 5 (WP-1, WP-2, WP-3) the application is **coherent**: what it shows is honest, what it claims is verified, and every open boundary is stated as a boundary. It becomes **complete for personal use** only when item 2's sequence (and, if wanted, items 3 and 4) is carried out under its own authorities.

### 16.16.6 `CV-41` disposition and how to reverse it

Two remedies were authorized for the placeholder-landing parents: repoint the parent at an implemented child, or mark it group-only. **Group-only was chosen** because repointing would make a group label silently mean “open this one child”, and because it fabricates nothing: `Research` keeps its `Company Intelligence` / `Cross-Sector Analytics` / `Sector Engines` children, `Intelligence` keeps `Decision Matrix`, `Evidence` was already a real destination and stays a link. Reversal is a one-line `navigation.ts` change per item with no fence, no route and no contract touched; the test asserting “every nav href resolves to a built surface” is what makes a careless reversal fail loudly rather than silently.

### 16.17.3 The end-to-end verdict, stated once

* Works: provider designation, the guarded read transport, dataset allow-listing, `NAS`/`CPI` parameter governance, `IIP` runtime enumeration and NIC-2 refusal logic, retry/backoff/timeout/pagination completeness rules, the fail-closed error taxonomy, the typed client, the state provider, and the live HTTP route.
* Connected to the product flow: **nothing user-facing.** There is no Macro route in `App.tsx`, no nav entry, and no view component; the provider's only consumer is its own test.
* Real-source data availability today, in this environment: **absent** (no egress). Historically the PA's evidence gate recorded unauthenticated `GET`s as live-confirmed, and that remains the recorded basis; nothing here re-derives or contradicts it.
* Therefore: **the capability is transport-complete and API-usable, and is not an exposed product capability.** No layer of this conclusion is inferred from another: the route answering is not proof of source data; a passing suite is not proof of a mounted screen; a mounted screen would still not be a qualified one.

## 16.18 CI verification record `CV-CORR-06` (`2026-10-14`; the IRR verification workflow implemented, published and green in hosted Actions — the IPD half remains outside)

*Added under the execution-authority directive of `2026-10-14` (the routine path — an
already-authorized repository change, recorded and self-verified, without re-asking). `CV-42`
required that a CI workflow be **proposed as a PR and not added silently**: that PR is PR #98 on
this branch, the change is published, and its checks are visible on GitHub. This section records
implementation only. It does not merge anything, and it changes no governance decision. Explicitly
excluded and unchanged: the **IPD** workflow half (it needs the §20 Stage 3 `P2`/`P3` main-admission
act), `iips-platform/**`, and the `frontend/server/macro/**`, Reports, User Portfolio and
owner-context surfaces.*

**16.18.1 What changed.**

| Path | Change | Why it is shaped this way |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | new | `name: CI`; `on: pull_request` (all) + `on: push: branches: [main]`; `permissions: contents: read`; `concurrency` per workflow+ref with `cancel-in-progress`; `timeout-minutes: 20`; one `ubuntu-latest` job, `working-directory: frontend`, with `defaults.run.shell: bash` so no step inherits a permissive shell |
| `frontend/.ci/assert-tests.js` | new | the zero-test guard. Reads only the Vitest JSON summary path given as its argument and fails unless `numTotalTests` is an integer `> 0`, `success` is `true`, `numFailedTests` is `0`, and at least one test file is recorded; a missing or malformed report is a **failure**, never a pass; a non-integer count is a failure. Pending/todo counts are reported but not enforced, so CI does not silently change the suite's disposition |
| `frontend/package.json` | `test:ci` added | `vitest run --reporter=default --reporter=json --outputFile.json=.vitest-report.json` — the *same* invocation as `test` plus a machine-readable summary for the guard. The existing `test` script is untouched, so no local or documented behaviour changes and no dependency is introduced (the flag belongs to Vitest itself) |
| `.gitignore` | one line added | `frontend/.vitest-report.json` — CI evidence is generated, never committed |

**16.18.2 Exact commands now run automatically**, in order, each failing the job on any non-zero exit
(no `continue-on-error`, no `|| true`, no `--passWithNoTests`, no fallback step anywhere in the file):

1. `actions/checkout@v4`
2. `actions/setup-node@v4` — `node-version: '22'`, `cache: npm`, `cache-dependency-path: frontend/package-lock.json`
3. `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` — reproducible install from `frontend/package-lock.json` (lockfile version 3, 259 packages)
4. `npm run typecheck` — the repository's established script (`tsc --noEmit`)
5. `npm run test:ci` — the complete Vitest suite
6. `node .ci/assert-tests.js .vitest-report.json` — the non-zero-discovery guard
7. `npm run build` — `tsc -b && vite build` (production build)

**Choices that are easy to get wrong, and their basis:** Node `22` and npm `10` are pinned because
they are the toolchain the recorded evidence was produced with (V3: Node v22.22.3, npm 10.9.8) —
the repository declares no `engines` and no `packageManager`, and adding a `packageManager` field
would imply Corepack and a different install path, so the runner controls both versions explicitly
instead. `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund` changes nothing about resolution; the flags only keep the log
short and stop a transient registry-metadata failure from looking like a broken build. **No secret,
token or credential is referenced** (verified: zero `secrets.` expressions in the file) because the
one GitHub-URL dependency, `iips-production-market-data` pinned to `git+https://github.com/ramkivs/iips-intelligent-portfolio-design.git#2e11fa3b…`, resolves from a **public** repository
(`gh api repos/…/ipd` → `private=false`), so a hosted runner can fetch it anonymously. **No
dependency pin was changed** to make CI pass, and none needed to be. `iips-platform/**` is
deliberately *not* added: it declares `typecheck: tsc --noEmit` and a `tsx --test` script, but that
tree is outside the established 705-test surface and folding it in here would change coverage
under the guise of tooling. The file also records, rather than fixes, that `frontend/tsconfig.json`
includes `src` + `vite.config.ts`, so the typecheck step covers the client while `server/**` is
exercised by the test step.

**16.18.7 What this result does *not* mean, and what is still outstanding.**
A green CI run proves that the established commands pass on the runner — it is not qualification, not

this area: (i) **branch protection / required checks** for `main` — a workflow that runs is not a
gate that blocks, and turning it into one is a repository-settings act belonging to the

requiring IPD `main` admission under §20 Stage 3; (iii) whether `iips-platform/**` should join CI, a

**16.19.4 The governed obligation chain — what `§16.17` lacked and what it now means.**
`D91` is established by a "constraint + disclosure act" whose commit **`727bdcb` is an IPD object**
(present in IPD, not an IRR object — verified: `git cat-file -t` fails in IRR, succeeds in IPD). Its
terms, as carried by three IRR `main` acts (`NP-08-D91-RELIEF-COMPETENCE-ESTABLISHMENT-ACT`,
`NP-08-D91-RELIEF-MECHANISM-ACT`, `NP-08-M5-D91-OUT-OF-SCOPE-DISPOSITION-ACT`): macro data is
**LIVE-only**, **EXEMPT** from the account-wide UI12 "Default data mode" preference, subject to a
**fallback prohibition**, and carries a **UI disclosure obligation on `MacroContext.tsx`** (D91 §1);
relief competence belongs to **D88** (`2dc5563` in IRR; `b607ea9` established competence);
**"No D91 relief is in force"**; `M-5` = "Relief from D91 (authority D88) for macro" and
`D91/D88_MACRO_RELIEF` **remains NOT GRANTED**; and macro **remains inside D8 Intelligence scope**
("`DEFERRED` does NOT mean `ABANDONED`"). Consequence, stated plainly: the disclosure obligation is
**operative and unmet on `main`** (the file renders nothing), while the implementations that would
discharge it sit unadmitted on L-B / L-C / L-E. That is a governance question about which authority
discharges which obligation — not an oversight to be closed by editing a component. Reusable facts for
the holder of the gate: `FreshnessBadge` (`frontend/src/components/ui/Badges.tsx`) and `EmptyState`
(`frontend/src/components/shell/ShellStates.tsx`) **already exist on `main`** and are what L-B's
rendering used.

## 16.29 CPI row-preservation remediation reconciled, validated, and live-verified on operator Windows evidence `CV-CORR-17` (`2026-10-15`; external + Arena evidence; no governed act amended, nothing merged)

**Why.** The `CV-CORR-05` finding in §16.17 — live source E2E `C — BLOCKED` — was a statement about **Arena's** egress, not about the provider: Arena's own probes ended in `000`/`SSL_ERROR_SYSCALL` and three browser requests returned `502` (V23). An egress-capable machine reported a real, reproducible failure on the CPI route. This section reconciles the two domains, records the remediation, and moves the live posture exactly as far as the evidence reaches.

### 16.29.1 The remediation — what actually failed, and what was changed

**Defect.** The CPI read path suppressed provider rows whose JSON was byte-identical to a row already seen, then compared the *surviving* count against the provider-declared record count and failed the whole retrieval when they differed. The live CPI payload legitimately contains exactly repeated rows — **152** of them in the month inspected — so a fully successful retrieval (259 pages, 25,884 rows, 25,884 declared) was reported as `INCOMPLETE_PAGINATION` and surfaced as `502`. The operator's report and the local arithmetic agree: `25,726` retained vs `25,884` declared is exactly the 158-row shortfall of the recorded reconstruction.

**Fix — five files, content-identical to the operator's verified copy** (established by SHA-256 identity, never by re-applying a patch):

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `frontend/server/macro/mospi-source.ts` | `FetchAllPagesOptions.deduplicate?: boolean` (default `true`); the absorber counts **every** received row in `rawRowsReceived` and suppresses duplicates **only when enabled**; `pagination` gains `recordsRetained` and `rawRowsReceived`; the completeness throw is dataset-neutral; the **CPI** call site passes `deduplicate: false` |
| `frontend/server/macro/mospi-source.test.ts` | The duplicate-suppression test was exercising **CPI** while asserting dedup — re-pointed at NAS; the two error-contract assertions reconciled onto the replacement message; new CPI retention test, CPI live-regression test (repeated rows, no false incomplete) and an explicit under-delivery test |
| `frontend/server/macro/macro-transport.ts` | Verified byte-identical to the TLS-only state **plus** the CPI call-site option |
| `frontend/server/macro/macro-transport.test.ts` | Route-level retention test |
| `frontend/src/api/macro.ts` | `recordsRetained` / `rawRowsReceived` carried into the client type |

**Invariants held, each re-checked this session.** Deduplication is disabled for CPI **explicitly and per call site**, never by default; the **default remains `true`**, so NAS and IIP behaviour is unchanged (neither call site passes the option); strict completeness is still enforced — `records.length !== expectedRecords` fails closed — and is now measured against the **provider-declared** count, so genuine under-delivery and inconsistent pagination still fail; identical CPI rows are retained; the page ceiling, bounded concurrency, and page-1 metadata/cross-page consistency checks are untouched; no unrelated route, dataset, TLS or architecture file was modified.

### 16.29.2 External evidence — operator Windows run (class: operator-transferred)

Source: `verify_live_mospi_cpi_iip.ps1` on the operator's Windows machine, isolated port `8788`, transferred in the session handoff; the same figures are recorded in the repository at `evidence/integration/mospi-live-e2e-windows-verification-2026-10-15/LIVE-VERIFICATION-RESULTS-2026-10-15.md`. **Arena did not execute this run and does not re-observe it.**

Direct control outside the application: `200`.
* **IIP — regression PASS.** HTTP `200`, `3/3` records, `COMPLETE` — the dedup default and the shared pagination path are unbroken on this leg.

### 16.29.7 Recorded, not actioned — CPI records without an `index` value (separate data-quality finding)

An independent inspection of the same live payload found that **996 of the `25,884` CPI records (≈3.8 %) carry no `index`**.

* **Not a pagination or row-preservation defect:** all `25,884` rows were received, retained and counted, and retrieval was declared `COMPLETE`. It is an observation about the **provider payload**.
* **Deliberately not folded into the remediation** (doing so would have silently changed the certified content). No code was written for it.
* **Existing coverage checked and absent:** a search of this tracker, the register and `docs/integration/**` found **no data-quality contract or work item** addressing provider-side field absence. The `DT-1…DT-15` criteria govern disclosure wording, placement, granularity and provenance honesty — not absent *values*. It is therefore opened here as a **distinct finding**, with no status row of its own yet.
* **Current application behaviour is already honest:** the field is typed optional (`readonly index?: string`), the mapper invents nothing, and the mounted CPI panel renders an absent value as an explicit `—`, never as a blank, a zero or a derived number. The D89 display contract is therefore not violated by the observation.
* **Smallest next action:** the PA decides (a) accept it as a provider characteristic with the `—` rendering recorded as sufficient, (b) raise it with MoSPI as a data-quality query, or (c) open a register item with its own acceptance criteria and evidence. Until then it stays recorded and **unscheduled**. **Disposed and CLOSED (`CV-CORR-23`, §16.35):** on `2026-10-16` the Program Authority selected **Option (a)** (`D-C` in `NP-08-D08-MACRO-VC6-L3-CPI-XV15-CONSOLIDATED-RECORD-01`) — the `996 / 25,884` null-`index` records are accepted as an upstream MoSPI payload characteristic, existing `'—'` rendering in `MacroResearch.tsx` is recorded as sufficient under `DT-8`, and this item is **CLOSED** with zero code changes and no external provider contact.

### 16.32.3 The obligation as IRR's own acts carry it, and the trigger that has fired

`D91 §1` is a **UI disclosure obligation on `MacroContext.tsx`** — a notice telling a user who selects `SNAPSHOT`/`PIT` that Macro does not switch modes (D91 competence act §5 items 3–4; mechanism act §7.1(4); packet §2). The mechanism act §18 records `D91 RELIEF — NOT GRANTED` and that "**No D91 relief is in force**", while "D91 remains fully operative: … the disclosure obligation all stand unchanged". The obligation is **conditional on a rendered Macro view** (packet §6.4(ii): where no view exists, no violation is observable and no compliance is demonstrable).

The Option E act's trigger **`R-1`** reads: *"A future authorised decision to implement a **rendered Macro view** (the D89 gate opens) … `DT-1`/`DT-2` and the D91 §1 notice attach to a view; at that moment disclosure ceases to be latent and **becomes mandatory**"*, with the standing note *"the deferral self-terminates on `R-1`"*. **`R-1` has fired on both branches:** the D89 gate opened (`CV-53-D89-MACRO-UI-DISCLOSURE-IMPLEMENTATION-AUTHORITY-DECISION-ACT-01`, PR #100) and a rendered view was implemented and mounted (PR #102, PR #103 at `main` `fd4ce609…`; accepted for the D89 display contract only in §16.27, PR #104). The consequence is recorded exactly as far as the corpus reaches: **the premise that kept the notice latent is gone**, the notice is absent at the rendered surface (C3/C5), and the D89 track **could not** have addressed it — `D89 §19` bounds its gate to "`DT-1–DT-8` and `DT-13/DT-15` **only**" and the CV-53 act's §5 limits that gate to surfaces "that render the **D89** disclosure".

### 16.32.4 The counter-fact on the IRR side — recorded, **not** adjudicated

`V-C5`'s notice is, by D91 §1's own subject matter, about a **UI12 `LIVE`/`SNAPSHOT`/`PIT` data-mode selection**. IRR has decided by Program Authority act that IRR may not offer that selection:

- **`NP-11-AUTH-01` §6 (`NP-11-D4`)**, `docs/integration/IIPS_v3.0_NP11_SETTINGS_PRODUCT_CONTRACT_AND_PERSISTENCE_OWNER_DESIGNATION.md`: *"**Decision: the historical donor's `LIVE / SNAPSHOT / PIT` user-selectable default data-mode preference is EXCLUDED FROM NP-11.** It is **not authorized** as a Settings preference"*; *"NP-11 must **not** provide a Settings control that changes: `LIVE/SNAPSHOT/PIT` selection; PIT addressing; data provenance; server-authoritative freshness; historical / as-of semantics"*; *"Any future proposal to make data mode user-configurable requires a **separate explicit governance decision** and must not be smuggled into NP-11"*; Decision Summary Matrix: `Data-mode / PIT preference · D4 · EXCLUDED`.
- **Premise drift recorded, not re-adjudicated:** `NP-11-D4`'s stated reason includes that the preference "depends on a **Macro surface that does not exist in IRR** (0 nav entries)" — a premise now dated (C4). Its other stated grounds (data mode/freshness/PIT/provenance are "governed / server-authoritative" behavior; the preference is "already **authority-blocked** (IPD inventory: *Authority-blocked: D91/D88 (macro, macro data-mode preference)*)") are unaffected. **`NP-11-D4` is not re-opened here.**
- **Enforcement at `main`:** C8/C9/C10 — `theme` is the only authorized preference key; the data-mode/PIT/freshness keys are rejected by validation and covered by rejecting tests; and no settings input can reach the Macro response path.

**The tension, stated without resolving it:** IRR's D91 acts say the obligation "**stands unchanged**" and, since `R-1` fired, record the notice as having "**become mandatory**" at a rendered view — while IRR's own governed UI12 contract **excludes the control the notice is about** and states that offering it needs a separate explicit governance decision. Rendering a notice that explains what happens "when you select `SNAPSHOT` or `PIT`" on a surface where no such selection exists, and none may be offered, would describe an affordance IRR's own contract prohibits. **Which governs the IRR state is a Program Authority determination, and the instrument that owns exactly this question already exists (Option 2 below).**

## 18 Capability Convergence Matrix (exact 17-column structure; one row per capability or cross-repository workstream)

**How to read.** Every cell judges **one dimension** independently and is never carried over from a neighbouring cell: implementation is not proof of integration, wiring, validation, acceptance, qualification or release readiness, and a passing automated suite is not product E2E or formal acceptance. Work-item detail stays in the register (§16.4); rows reference `CV-*`/`XV-*` IDs instead of restating it. `V1`…`V72` are the executed checks indexed in §§16.3 and 16.14–16.49 and are the primary evidence anchors; `NA` is used only where the dimension genuinely cannot apply.

**Status legend.** Workbook vocabulary: `V` VERIFIED (executed or directly inspected here) · `I` IMPLEMENTED · `P` PARTIAL · `NI` NOT INTEGRATED (exists, no consumer on the authoritative ref) · `NW` NOT WIRED (no route or UI) · `NP` NOT PERSISTED · `VP` VALIDATION PENDING · `EP` E2E PENDING · `EM` EVIDENCE MISSING · `AP` AUTHORITY PENDING · `BL` BLOCKED · `UR` UNRESOLVED · `NA` NOT APPLICABLE · `OOS` OUT OF SCOPE. Extra values kept distinct because the vocabulary alone would merge materially different states: `DEFERRED` (a dated decision says so) · `NOT SATISFIED` (a named bar exists and is not met) · `NOT ESTABLISHED` (no authorized determination/evidence exists) · `NOT AUTHORIZED` / `AUTHORITY WITHHELD` (an express prohibition in a governed record) · `RECOVERY UNPROVEN`, written `VP — … off-main` where a proof exists but not on `main` · `SOURCE-REPORTED` (asserted by a record this session did not re-execute — e.g. the Windows-only shell acceptance, the `G24` `84/84` live suite, the v1.1 certificates). A `SOURCE-REPORTED` cell must not be re-labelled `V` without executing it.

## 20 Ordered Convergence Progression (dependency-ordered; no stage blocks an unrelated capability)

**Rule.** Stages 1–3 and 7 are **authorized now**; Stages 4–6 are **decision gates** whose planning is authorized while their implementation is not — planning a stage never authorizes building it, and the only authority source is the record named in "Authority Required". The one ordering constraint the evidence supports is `Stage 4 → Stage 5`, and inside Stage 5 the order is fixed too: implementation (only if authorized) → qualification → admission by its own act; a qualified-but-unadmitted line is a legitimate end state for this cycle. Nothing makes Reports, universe coverage, pin durability, CI, the runbook or documentation wait behind the portfolio decision, so they run in parallel; §16.5’s four chains, not a single critical path, are the real shape.

The accepted Gate E W-1 policy remains exact and conjunctive. A write (`portfolio.create`, `portfolio.save`, `portfolio.reset`, or `portfolio.delete`) may succeed only when **all four** conditions hold:

1. the Gate E policy is accepted by the PA;

4. a Gate 5 admission act names the qualified IPD and IRR commits and lifts the IRR `503` fence for the named operations.

Otherwise IPD refuses/returns `WRITE_NOT_AUTHORIZED` (or an earlier refusal) with **zero store mutations**. Current condition status: W-1(1) is accepted; W-1(2) is not effective because the companion act is proposed and its exact IPD file/test set remains unpinned; W-1(3) is not executed/accepted; W-1(4) is not granted. `3b` is not a write enablement.

### 16.67.3 Method and counting rules

1. **Row-by-row derivation.** Each row's 17 cells were re-judged individually against the evidence listed in its anchor. No cell was carried over from a neighbouring cell, and no cell was upgraded because the tracker, a prior report, a merged document or a green CI said so.
2. **Evidence classes kept separate.** *Executed this pass* (tests, build, typecheck, hashes, ancestry, API reads) · *independently inspected* (code, records, refs) · *source-reported / operator-transferred* (Windows runs, `G24 84/84`, v1.1/N4 certificates). Only the first two may move a cell to `V`.
3. **Status vocabulary.** The §18 legend is used unchanged (`V`, `I`, `P`, `NI`, `NW`, `NP`, `VP`, `EP`, `EM`, `AP`, `BL`, `UR`, `NA`, `OOS`, `DEFERRED`, `NOT SATISFIED`, `NOT ESTABLISHED`, `NOT AUTHORIZED`, `SOURCE-REPORTED`). No new token is introduced. Where the legend cannot express a state, the cell spells the qualification out in words rather than inventing a code.
4. **Row outcome (summary only).** One primary outcome is assigned per row, with this precedence: **(a)** a dated act defers, excludes or declines the row's product scope — in whole or for a named slice → **DEFERRED / OUT OF SCOPE**; **(b)** an in-scope dimension requires a decision, admission or act that does not exist → **PENDING / BLOCKED**; **(c)** an in-scope dimension is unsatisfied but executable within existing authority → **PARTIAL**; **(d)** otherwise → **COMPLETE within recorded scope**. The outcome is a *summary of the cells*, never a substitute for them: a row can be COMPLETE for its recorded scope while its release-readiness cell stays `P` or `NA`.
5. **Counts.** §16.12 counts register **items** (`CV-*`); §18 counts **capability rows**. They are different populations and are not expected to sum to each other: the 51 rows include deferred, out-of-scope, historical and governance workstreams that have no register item, and several register items (e.g. `CV-25`, `CV-35`, `CV-42`) are not capability rows.
6. **Minimal coherent change.** Historical text was preserved; corrections are additive, dated and attributed, with the superseded value quoted wherever a number or status changed.

**Files added (test-only; zero product-code change):**

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `frontend/server/persistence/consumer-restart-writer.ts` | Process A child: runs the REAL consumer commands (watchlists: create+add-item with governed baseline & trigger; collaboration: create thread + add comment with resolved refs and vintage pin; settings: update owner A, update+**reset** owner B), read-back-verifies, asserts its journal bytes, terminates |

**Semantics proven per row:** row 9 — the watchlist, its item's governed baseline (`close 1234.5`, `asOf`), trigger set and timestamps read back identically in a new process; row 10 — the thread, anchor, NS-5 vintage pin, comment body/refs/authorship read back identically; row 11 — the surviving update (owner A: `dark`, revision 1, `settings-updated`) **and** the reset (owner B: governed default `light`, revision **2**, `settings-reset`) both read back — the reset survives restart as a NEW revision with history preserved, never as a rewrite.

### 16.70.4 Interpretation established

- **R-1 — Project-wide, not re-asked.** The grant covers necessary decisions, implementation, testing, corrections and publication within established scope, and forbids repeated approval for individual decisions or routine steps. Its only textual limits are its four exclusions.
- **R-2 — Established scope is set by PA product decisions.** For P11 that scope was set by the bounded-library disposition, which **expressly includes** the momentum-propagation and effective-input lineage fixes — i.e. the candidate's content. What was not settled was branch membership of that content; a bounded admission act settles exactly that.
- **R-3 — Authorization ≠ act ≠ proof.** Authorization (the grant; §16.70) permits the act without a new approval round; the act (the IPD `D-06` record) records the disposition; proof (remote ancestry + blob identity) is the only thing that establishes that admission occurred.
- **R-4 — §16.65.4 preserved; its scope fixed.** Original text retained verbatim (§16.65.4 now carries a dated interpretation pointer). The "prove" clause is reaffirmed permanently; the "authorize" clause is an anti-inference rule; the "execution ceiling" attributed to handoff §2 is **superseded as a general ceiling only**. `CHG-2026-10-15-04`'s broader reading is preserved as dated history and not carried forward; acts it governed are unaffected because each was separately authorized when taken.
- **R-5 — Acceptance ≠ admission (unchanged).** §16.65 accepted a capability claim and said so; the admission bar is an explicit, evidence-bound act naming exact commits.
- **R-6 — No record may imply an admission it did not perform.** §16.69.3's statement remains correct for that record and for this one; it is an anti-implication rule, not a finding that admission is unavailable.
- **R-7 — Capacity.** IRR determines authority; the IPD capacity acts and proves. An IRR record announcing IPD `main` membership would assert a fact its repository cannot prove.
- **R-8 — No widening of restrictions.** S3's "prove" clause is not widened into per-merge approval; §16.65's bounded caveats are not widened into "no P11 code may enter `main`"; conversely this determination is not widened beyond §16.70.6–§16.70.8.

## §16.73 — `CV-CORR-54`: Gate 3 IPC connection-release correction (`2026-10-21`; renumbered from colliding `16.69` / `CV-CORR-52` in §16.74)

Executed repository-side remediation of the native-Windows IPC defect. This section records executed work and verified facts only. It renders no Gate 3 acceptance, admits nothing, and lifts no fence. *(Numbering note, `2026-10-22`, §16.74: originally merged after §16.70 under duplicate heading `## 16.69 Gate 3 IPC connection-release correction (CV-CORR-52, 2026-10-21)`; re-identified as `§16.73` / `CV-CORR-54` to preserve established `§16.69` / `CV-CORR-52` [CV-36] and `§16.70` / `CV-CORR-53` [DEC-06] intact without substantive change.)*

### 16.73.1 Root cause (proven, not inferred)

| Fact | Evidence |
|---|---|
| Capacity is one | `src/ipc/endpoint.ts` `listenIpc`: `server.maxConnections = options.maxConnections ?? 1` (C5.4) |
| Node releases a slot only on destruction | `lib/net.js` `Socket.prototype._destroy`: `this._server._connections--` — the sole decrement; `end()`, FIN and peer disconnect do not release it |
| The check precedes the handler | `lib/net.js onconnection`: `if (self.maxConnections != null && self._connections >= self.maxConnections) { … clientHandle.close(); return; }` — returns **before** `self.emit('connection', socket)` |
| The flush-guard path never closed the handle | `3eb13ed` wrote the response with `socket.end(frame)`; `libuv/src/win/pipe.c` `uv__pipe_shutdown` is a `FlushFileBuffers` with no half-close primitive |

Consequence: the first request of a server lifetime succeeded and every subsequent connection was dropped by the runtime before the handler existed → **zero bytes**. This explains the reported 9 pass / 1 fail whole-file run versus a 1/1 name-filtered run (filtering removes the earlier IPC calls that consumed the slot), with normal exit and no timeout.

### 16.73.2 Contract decision (act-sourced)

Governing text: act §4.2 item 11 (protocol — "one request and at most one response per connection; pipelined frames refused"); §4.2 item 13 (dispatch — "Class P refusals with zero bytes and connection close"); §4.3 row `tests/g3_ipc_framing.test.ts` (T-A — zero bytes and connection close for oversize/malformed/`v ≠ 1`/unknown `op`/truncated/pipelined frames, plus sink-only audit assertions); request §6.2 row T-A ("Zero bytes; connection closed (Class P)"). `IRR PKG-11 §E` and `PKG-12` are **not present as documents in either repository** and were not relied upon; no rule was invented in their absence.

- **Pre-flush second frame** — zero bytes, connection closed, `MALFORMED_FRAME` in the bounded sink. **Unchanged**; this is the case T-A governs.
- **Post-flush second frame** — the response is legitimate and delivered; the handle is closed, so the frame cannot reach the server. The one-frame invariant is enforced **structurally**: exactly one response, the second frame never dispatched, no second response. Zero-byte refusal cannot apply, and a post-flush sink record is unobservable.
- **Unreachable frame (connection closed)** — satisfied by non-existence of the connection, a stronger guarantee than observing the frame.

Rationale for yielding the post-flush diagnostic: observing it requires an open handle, which consumes the only capacity slot; a bounded window would hold the slot and drop a promptly-following request, reinstating the defect. Capacity release is required behaviour. Recorded as a design decision under the act citations above — **not** a protocol change and **not** a weakening of the pre-flush guarantees.

### 16.73.3 Implementation (within the act manifest)

| Path | Basis | Change |
|---|---|---|
| `src/ipc/dispatch.ts` | §4.2 item 13 | Flush-guard response written via `writeFrame` (`socket.write`) instead of `endFrame`; handle **closed as soon as the frame flushes**; `attachPostFlushWatch` and the unused `responded` flag removed; `finally` closes any remaining flush-guard exit |
| `tests/g3_ipc_framing.test.ts` | §4.3 T-A | Three emulation assertions re-pointed from "socket stays open" to "handle released"; real-socket Windows branch asserts exactly one response frame and no second response bytes |
| `tests/g3_binding_resolution.test.ts` | §4.3 T-C | New describe: five sequential requests across one server lifetime, capacity released to zero, recovery after a zero-byte Class P refusal |

**No new file** (act §4.3 fixes the set at 8). `scripts/run-tests.mjs`, `ci.yml` and all endpoints, startup and persistence sources are untouched.

### 16.73.4 Validation (POSIX — not native Windows)

`npx tsc` exit `0`; `npx vite build` success; `npm test` → `# tests 754`, `# pass 753`, `# fail 0`, `# skipped 1`, 95 suites, `[test-guard] OK`; `node --test dist/tests/g3_*.test.js` → `198 / 197 / 0 / 1`; `g3_binding_resolution` `13/13`; `g3_ipc_framing` `30/30`; flush-guard sequential probe with the Windows policy forced on AF_UNIX → 5/5 served, `accepted = closed = 5`, `getConnections() = 0`. The emulation suite fails **3** tests against unmodified `3eb13ed` and passes with the correction.

**Limitation recorded:** the new T-C sequential tests also pass on the base *on Linux*, because AF_UNIX `end()` closes the socket; they are not a POSIX discriminator for the leak. The POSIX discriminator is the emulation suite; the T-C tests are the native-Windows regression and a guard against a return to write-without-close.

### 16.73.5 Publication

Candidate commit `5fb7efe7b50b73d90651b09bfe2bdd4ff7210787` on `g3/gate3-node-sqlite-ipc-correction-d30003d` (parent `3eb13ed`). **Not published to the IPD remote:** the active App installation token lacks `contents:write` on `ramkivs/iips-production-market-data` — `git push` returns `403 Permission … denied to ramkivs` and API ref creation returns `403 Resource not accessible by integration`, while the same token writes `ramkivs/iips-review-recovered` (probe ref created and deleted). **IPD PR #34 is unchanged.** Artifact `docs/integration/artifacts/g3-connection-release.patch`, `18,900` B, SHA-256 `5745647e32b1da67fb984a7748406921aefb495000dfcbfdd9255133cad5fe0a`, `git apply --check` clean against `3eb13ed`, reproduces the commit byte-for-byte, and rebuilds to `198 / 197 / 0 / 1` independently.

`g3-flush-guard-release.patch` (`a9e0ebd6…`) is **SUPERSEDED**: it added a ninth test file outside the act's fixed set and asserted connection counts without synchronising on the release signal (the operator's *Failure A*). The operator's *Failure B* is independent of both candidates — the framing suite builds its own handler and has never recorded a post-flush diagnostic; IPD PR #34's body already records that test failing at `3eb13ed` with `MALFORMED_FRAME` expected / `undefined` received.

(2) Confirmation that the peer drains the buffered frame before `ERROR_BROKEN_PIPE` after the handle is closed (expected by Windows pipe semantics; unobserved here). (3) Full transcript including the four Windows-skipped test names. (4) The Windows `src/ipc/dispatch.ts` remains a 16,153-byte local file of unverified content; the artifact applies to `3eb13ed`, not to that working tree.

**Gate 3 remains BLOCKED / NOT ACCEPTED** — native-Windows acceptance is outstanding and operator-owned. No merge is authorized.

*End of §16.73.*

The pre-flush pipelined refusal (zero bytes, close, `MALFORMED_FRAME` in the sink) is **unchanged**. Retaining a post-flush record needs an open handle, which consumes the only C5.4 slot and reinstates the defect | act §4.3 T-A, §4.2 item 11 |

### 16.76.3 The defect and the correction — connection-slot release

The defect is real, is specific, and is carried in a two-file diff:

- **Inherited defect.** On the `flush-guard` settlement path — the Windows named-pipe transport — the single response was written with `endFrame()`, which half-closes the writable side but **leaves the libuv handle open**. `listenIpc` sets `server.maxConnections = 1` (contract C5.4), and Node decrements `server._connections` only on `Socket._destroy`. The slot therefore stayed consumed for the server's lifetime, and **every later connection was dropped before `'connection'` fired**. The prior mitigation — a post-flush watchdog that recorded `MALFORMED_FRAME` and called `socket.destroy()` — observed the problem instead of releasing the slot.
- **Correction adopted in `afa4309…`** (`src/ipc/dispatch.ts`, blob `827f7d78… → 6c8fcbc8…`): write the frame **without** half-close (`writeFrame()`), then `socket.destroy()` **explicitly** on the flush-guard path, so the capacity slot is released as soon as the response has flushed. The post-flush watchdog is removed; the one-frame invariant becomes *structural* — with the handle closed, a second frame cannot reach a handler at all.
- **Recorded semantic change (not a defect claim, and not a regression to be inferred).** The post-flush `MALFORMED_FRAME` **diagnostic record** no longer exists on that path; refusal is now silent-but-total rather than recorded-and-torn-down. The behaviour required by contract T-A — *pipelined frame before the response ⇒ zero bytes and Class P refusal* — is unchanged and still asserted. Any future reader who expected a post-flush sink entry will not find one, and that is the intended trade.
- **Independently reproduced in this pass** (§16.76.10 `V202`): `afa4309…`'s targeted suites pass **44/44**; the same post-fix suites executed against the **pre-fix** source (`54123307…`) pass **40** and fail **4**, all four in the flush-guard settlement suite. The pre-fix tree carries only the older **41**-test inventory, so *"44 tests / 40 pass / 4 fail"* was never a committed state — it is a cross-version experiment, and it is recorded here as exactly that.

### 16.81.3 GOV-03 — implementation gaps found by inspection

1. **No durable path from broker import.** `BrokerImportModal` → `BrokerImportIngressOrchestrator` → `SessionPortfolioStorePort` → the in-memory `PortfolioStore`. The durable store and the IPC endpoint existed on IPD `main` but no import path reached them — the exact CV-39 wording ("durable persistence … without yet wiring `PortfolioStore`/broker import").
2. **No identity gate on the durable path.** `DurablePortfolioStore.validate()` persisted any holding vector handed to it; the Gate E W-6 / DP-2 2F rule had no implementation there (the recorded Gate 4 limitation fact *G-13 / V261*).
3. **The contribution ledger was never written.** `portfolio_contributions` existed in migration 001 but was never inserted into or read from; the W-8 / BI-08 duplicate rule therefore could not be evaluated, and the duplicate check compared only the **newest** revision's content digest — so re-importing an **earlier** broker file was applied a second time (the "unintended duplication" failure mode named in CV-39).
4. **The durable read projections did not carry the contract v1 §6 shapes** (`PortfolioSummary` / `PortfolioDetail`).
5. **The IPC read wire departed from contract v1 §6 in two further ways, both pre-existing at `1cceacff…`**: every read result was **wrapped** (`{ portfolios: [...] }`, `{ portfolio: {...} }`, `{ revisions: [...] }`) where contract v1 §6 fixes the result as `PortfolioSummary[]` / `PortfolioDetail` / `RevisionEntry[]`; and the revision timestamp was named `createdAt` where contract v1 §6 and the effective Gate 3 act both fix `committedAt`. The frozen IRR consumer adapter refuses both shapes, so **no conforming read could ever reach the Row 30 read surfaces**.

### 16.83.3 Existing persistence is not the product UI path

The browser import modal defaults to `SessionPortfolioStorePort` (`durable:false`) and calls `confirmAndSaveViaPort`. No frontend fetch/API/native/IPC bridge or IPD host/preload was found. `persistBrokerImport` has no product caller; positive commit/restart tests call it directly on disposable `DurablePortfolioStore` fixtures. `src/ipc/protocol.ts` defines `portfolio.save`, but the dispatcher returns `WRITE_NOT_AUTHORIZED` for every write before mutation and implements reads only. The current UI and the IPD SQLite store are therefore unconnected.

The v1 contract’s client is the IRR server process; it defines `portfolio.save` but authorizes no writes and does not authorize IPD browser calls. It requires raw broker-observed fields and IPD-side identity resolution, refusing caller-supplied identity claims. The current broker-import helper checks supplied `companyId`/identity status/disposition instead of resolving raw identifiers itself, so it is not a compliant IPC handler. Current portfolio mutations lack an explicit multi-statement transaction; the fixture restart tests do not prove rollback, crash atomicity, or a product UI/IPC round trip. Existing metadata mapping is incomplete, including `importedAt` and contribution provenance; no schema/mapping change is made.

### 16.83.4 Transport direction prepared, not decided or implemented

The narrowest future candidate is a **trusted host-owned bridge** from the existing UI store-port seam into the IPD-owned same-host IPC endpoint, reusing the v1 `portfolio.save` wire shape only if all required fields fit without changing semantics. The current accepted contract’s IRR-client scope does not authorize this caller; a separate PA decision must explicitly authorize the IPD UI host/bridge. The host/runtime and exact bridge files are absent from IPD `main` and must be identified before a manifest can be named.

Direct browser socket access is not viable; a new HTTP/TCP listener conflicts with the current contract/endpoint; a new `broker.import` write operation needs a major contract/Gate E revision; routing through IRR/503 surfaces is excluded from CAP-02. This is a recommendation only, not implementation authority.

### 16.83.7 Refined transport conclusion and narrowest future boundary

The frontend `PortfolioStorePort` and backend `DurablePortfolioStorePort` are not drop-in compatible: the UI requires `getPortfolio`/`getAnalytics`/`getRevision` and a full asynchronous UI save result; the backend exposes owner-scoped Node/SQLite store methods. Accepted v1 reserves `portfolio.analytics`, and v1 `portfolio.save` returns only disposition/revision/durability fields rather than the UI's full `PortfolioSaveResult`. No adapter may fabricate analytics, portfolio, save counters, timestamps, provenance or durability.

IRR's real `callIpc` and `IpcUserPortfolioPort` remain outside the IPD UI and unwired behind all twelve HTTP 503 route-method pairs. The client is useful host-side evidence (one connection/request, no automatic write retry, outcome-unknown on timeout), not a working CAP-02 bridge. Its adapter strips canonical/lineage/weight fields, throws an envelope-gap error after any upstream save success, emits an `options` bag whose shape differs from v1's declared top-level save fields, and can omit W-5-mandatory `expectedRevision`; it cannot be copied unchanged as proof of wire conformance.

The prior conditional same-host IPC preference is therefore refined as follows:

- **Recommended now:** defer source implementation and preserve the session-only UI, W-1 refusal and every 503 fence.
- **Required next governance decision:** reconcile CAP-02 with G1-B1. If G1 remains, any IRR-host integration is separately scoped and admitted, not a hidden CAP-02/IRR-route dependency. If an IPD-local application host is desired, the PA must expressly establish that exception, its owner/runtime, and exact new files/tests.
- **Conditional future transport only:** after that decision, a narrowly typed host-mediated adapter to the existing IPD same-host IPC endpoint is narrower than a new network listener or new write operation. Reuse v1 `portfolio.save` only if raw observations, mandatory revision and provenance fit exactly; v1 alone does not satisfy the complete UI port.
- **Narrowest credible future transport manifest:** one owned host composition root/lifecycle, one typed host IPC client, one least-privilege renderer bridge, one complete adapter injected at the existing workspace `storePort` seam, and reuse of the existing IPD startup/endpoint/dispatch. Exact new host/bridge filenames remain unresolved and must not be fabricated.
- **Separate write boundary:** IPD-side raw-identity resolution, complete file/import-time/contribution provenance, one immediate transaction including binding revalidation and every mutation, idempotency/concurrency, outcome-unknown reconciliation, and real UI-to-socket tests require a later effective write act. Direct in-process store/helper shortcuts do not bypass these requirements.

Transaction gaps remain source-proven: binding resolution's separate immediate transaction does not surround the later mutation; store create/save/revision/contribution statements have no enclosing request transaction; and the helper's list-then-write sequence is not concurrency/atomicity proof. Gate A′ remains unexecuted and its approved basis incompatible with current provisioning/schema. Gate 4 remains **PROPOSED / NOT EFFECTIVE / NOT STARTED**, with target-host QE and separate result acceptance outstanding; Gate 5 remains not granted/initiated. No hosted CI or fixture result changes those states.

### 16.84.3 Prepared topology/ownership disposition (proposed only)

The record's §3 sets out six items for PA determination. In condensed form, **if accepted** they would:

1. retain **IRR** as the integrated IIPS product/application host under G1-B1;
2. retain **IPD** as the owner of durable portfolio persistence and its same-host IPC interface;
3. decline to create an **independent IPD-local native application host** as an assumed CAP-02 prerequisite;
4. require any future renderer-to-IPD integration to identify its **actual host composition root, lifecycle owner, bridge boundary and exact implementation files** before implementation authorization;
5. keep **transport implementation, durable-write correctness, Gate 4 qualification and result acceptance, Gate 5 admission and operational write authorization** as distinct decisions or prerequisites; and
6. preserve **all existing write-denial behaviour and IRR HTTP `503` fences** until the relevant authorities and gates permit a change.

This resolves the ownership question the CAP-02-HOST-01 investigation left **UNRESOLVED** — not by inventing a second host, but by declining to assume one. It does **not** select a host composition root, a bridge technology, a caller, a wire change or an implementation manifest, and it does **not** convert CAP-02 into an IRR/CAP-03 route dependency. Any future IRR-host path is separately scoped and separately admitted.

The decision adopts the six prepared items **without amendment**:

2. IPD retained as owner of durable portfolio persistence and its same-host IPC interface;

5. transport implementation, durable-write correctness, Gate 4 qualification and result acceptance, Gate 5 admission and operational write authorization remain distinct decisions or prerequisites;
6. all existing write-denial behaviour and IRR HTTP `503` fences are preserved until the relevant authorities and gates permit a change.

   `frontend/src/app/**` shell is not promoted to a second product host;

   identity resolution, provenance and lineage digests, consolidation arithmetic and persistence; IRR owns

### 16.86.4 Why this placement, on repository evidence

| Option | Determination | Grounds verified this pass |
|---|---|---|
| **A — move UI into IRR** | **Rejected** | IRR has no security-master/quarantine/provenance/consolidation module at all, so the 4,894-line component set cannot run there without the domain; a move relocates IPD domain into the repository G1-B1 says is *not* authoritative for it; **G-2 §1(2)** requires "extend, not replace or duplicate" and §2 lists *"SecurityMaster and canonical company-identity mapping"* among IPD capability to preserve and reuse; the effective store-port act authorizes the files by exact **IPD** path |
| **B — IPD-local host** | **Rejected** | Contradicts effective topology item 3 and G1-B1 item 1; no native host, preload, `contextBridge` or launch composition exists in either repository; IPD has a Vite shell and no server; a browser UI still cannot reach IPD's `node:net` endpoint, so a new listener or a non-existent native bridge would be required — the transport would remain unsolved after reversing an effective decision |
| **C — IPD-authored, IRR-hosted** | **SELECTED** | Consistent with G1-B1, G-2 §1(2)–(3), topology items 1–3 and the store-port act's own stated purpose; IRR already owns the host, routing, navigation and the tested (unwired) IPC client; the port is the designed inversion point; no domain is rewritten; the whole path is testable through refusal |
| **D1 — import into IRR's certified reference portfolio** | **Rejected** | Wrong domain: `/api/portfolio` is the certified reference workspace, explicitly distinct from the user portfolio (**G-2 §1(4)**); no write path, no holdings store |
| **D2 — serve IPD's Vite app from the IRR origin** | **Rejected** | Requires IPD's dev server as a second host (same defect as B); an ungoverned cross-origin frame carrying broker files; no record supports it |
| **D3 — new `broker.import` IPC operation** | **Preserved, not selected** | Not an existing composition; the closed v1 set excludes it and §16.83 already found a new write operation needs a major contract/Gate E revision; recorded as the documented future variant so a later reader sees it was considered |

**A and C are not the same option differently implemented.** A relocates authorship and domain ownership;
C relocates neither and crosses the repository boundary only with an *exported consumable surface* and IRR's
own port implementation.

### 16.92.4 Phase D/E/F — Modal/Port Integration, Revision-Read Route, Safeguards & Evidence Classification (`PR #227`)

1. **Server v1 revision-read adapter & HTTP route (`frontend/server/broker-import/{brokerImportV1SaveAdapter.ts,brokerImportHttp.ts,index.ts}`):**
   - `readBrokerImportRevisionViaV1`: dispatches `callIpc('portfolio.list', {}, {})`, validates `PortfolioSummary[]`, and returns `{ portfolioId, revision: matching.currentRevision, exists: true }` or `{ portfolioId, revision: null, exists: false }`, projecting only `portfolioId` and `currentRevision` (`name` and `updatedAt` discarded at server boundary).
   - `GET /api/broker-import/:portfolioId/revision`: admitted read-only endpoint under the existing `/api/broker-import` prefix; enforces the fail-closed `isIpcBindingPreconditionSatisfied()` gate (`503 owner-context-unavailable` before any adapter/IPC call when absent), refuses cross-site `Origin`/`Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` (`403`), sets `Allow: GET, POST` on `405` for `/holdings`, and maps Class P (`BINDING_ABSENT`) to the identical `503 owner-context-unavailable` body (`IRR-2`).
2. **Browser API client & IRR `PortfolioStorePort` adapter (`frontend/src/api/brokerImport.ts`, `frontend/src/features/portfolio-import/irrPortfolioStorePortAdapter.ts`):**
   - `readBrokerImportRevision`: relative-URL `GET /api/broker-import/:portfolioId/revision` returning `{ status: 'OK', portfolioId, revision, exists }` or `{ status: 'REFUSED' | 'OUTCOME_UNKNOWN', ... }`.
   - `IrrBrokerImportStorePortAdapter`: implements `PortfolioStorePort` from `iips-production-market-data/portfolio-ui`; declares static `{ persistenceMode: 'SESSION_ONLY', durable: false }`; delegates `savePortfolio(request)` to `submitBrokerImportHoldings` with zero retries, relaying `SAVED` (`PortfolioCommitReceipt` verbatim), `REFUSED` (`PortfolioPortRefusal` with `storeEffect: 'NONE'`), or `OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` (`reconcileRevisionReadAvailable: true`); implements `readPortfolio(portfolioId)` via `readBrokerImportRevision` returning a revision-only `UserPortfolioRecord` carrier (`holdings: []`, `revisionHistory: []`, empty timestamps) when `exists: true` or `null` when `exists: false`, and throwing on `REFUSED`/`OUTCOME_UNKNOWN` so the modal's `catch` keeps the revision check unresolved without fabricating `Revision 0`; explicitly refuses `listPortfolios`, `deletePortfolio`, and `getRevisionHistory`.
3. **Host mount (`frontend/src/features/portfolio-import/BrokerImportSurface.tsx`, `frontend/src/app/App.tsx`):**
   - Mounts `BrokerImportModal` from `iips-production-market-data/portfolio-ui` at `/user-portfolios/import` with governed empty `SecurityMaster` (`new SecurityMaster([])`) and `IrrBrokerImportStorePortAdapter`.

### 16.113.2 Key `CV-51` Readiness Findings

Full evidence-backed answers to all 11 investigation questions (`Q1`–`Q11`) are published in [`docs/integration/IIPS_v3.0_REPORTS_NP06_CV51_READINESS_INVESTIGATION_AND_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-10-25.md`](docs/integration/IIPS_v3.0_REPORTS_NP06_CV51_READINESS_INVESTIGATION_AND_IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN_2026-10-25.md) (`IIPS-V3-REPORTS-NP06-CV51-READINESS-AND-PLAN-2026-10-25-01`):

1. **Zero Technical / Backend Blockers for Read-Only Exposure (`Option CV51-A`):** All four `GET` endpoints (`GET /api/reports/context`, `GET /api/reports/artifacts?limit=&cursor=`, `GET /api/reports/artifacts/:reportId`, `GET /api/reports/artifacts/:reportId/supersession`) are live, loopback-proxied (`vite.config.ts:18`), C8-hardened (`executive-transport.ts:716,974`), and `F-7`-qualified across separate OS processes, mapping 1:1 onto all four `NP-06 D8` / `§5.6` progressive-disclosure levels (`Summary`, `Detail`, `Evidence & Provenance`, `Replay & Reference`).
2. **Why `POST` Creation/Append UI Is Excluded from Minimum Scope:** `POST /api/reports/artifacts*` requires a caller-supplied `FrozenReportingEngineOutput`, which no HTTP read route on `executive-transport.ts` exposes and which React is prohibited from synthesizing client-side (`NP-06 G11`/`R5`, `design-principles.md` §2). Adding server-side CSIP report-generation triggers would expand backend scope and reopen `R2`/`F-7`. Read-only `Option CV51-A` (matching `G-2` `UserPortfolioList`/`UserPortfolioDetail`, `CV-53`, and `PKG-08 Row 4`) preserves 100% of completed backend gates untouched.
3. **Two Critical Source-Verified Safeguards Built Into the Implementation Plan:**
   - `GET /api/reports/context` returns `200` when `IIPS_REPORTS_OWNER_PATH` is valid even if `IIPS_NP04_DATABASE_PATH` is unset (`reports-transport.ts:198-215`); therefore `/reports` evaluates availability directly from `GET /api/reports/artifacts`.
   - `reports-transport.ts:159` (`reason: error.message` on `PersistenceBoundaryError`) and `executive-transport.ts:761` (`detail: String(e)` on mount `500`) are stripped in `frontend/src/api/reports.ts` via a closed client failure vocabulary (`ReportsFailureKind`), and wire `tenantId`/`ownerUserId` partition literals are stripped before view-model construction (matching `F-3` Browser Acceptance §5).
4. **Sole Immediate Blocker Is Governance Authority:** Only explicit PA approval of the companion proposed decision act (`IIPS-V3-REPORTS-NP06-CV51-UI-EXPOSURE-PA-DECISION-ACT-2026-10-25-01`) stands before bounded UI implementation may execute.
